tabs.title: Form Responses 1
headers: Talking to many people at parties really energizes you.
You find it easy to spend time alone, without any other people.
You find it relatively easy to initiate conversations with others.
Attending a large, crowded festival leaves you feeling exhausted and drained, rather than energized.
At a social event, you are likely to strike up a conversation with someone interesting even if you don’t know them.
When waiting in a room with just one other person, they usually start talking first.
You prefer going out with a group of friends or acquaintances rather than with a single friend or alone.
After an exhausting workweek, you would rather chill out and relax at home than go out and blow off some steam.
At parties and similar events, you like to be close to where the action is.
You prefer spending time with your friends one-on-one rather than in a group setting.
You are less interested in the raw facts than in the big picture.
In most things, you are more of a practitioner than a theoretician.
You often enjoy venturing into speculation.
You would be content with knowing the solution to a problem without understanding the reasoning behind it.
You believe that the real truth is not visible from the facts on the surface.
You tend to stick to the tried and tested and do not waste energy on exploring new options and alternatives.
You love engaging in conversation about where science and technology will take humanity next.
You do not like to delve into abstract topics.
You tend to see your friends not in light of what they currently are, but what they could become.
You tend to be suspicious of and not trust anything that challenges common sense.
When it comes to ensuring your team achieves its goals, pushing for the best solution is more important than being cooperative.
Even if you disagree with someone, you try hard not to hurt their feelings.
You think telling the truth is more important than taking care not to hurt someone.
You are more likely to provide emotional support than suggest ways of dealing with the problem.
If a member of your team had serious trouble keeping up and pulling their own weight, you would vote to replace them.
If you had a business, you would find it very difficult to fire loyal but underperforming employees.
Giving useful advice to someone in a tough situation is more important than making them feel better.
You tend to feel the problems of those close to you as if they were your own.
People need to act rationally to earn your respect.
Being too pragmatic is much worse than being too passionate.
You work best when you have a clear plan set out before you.
You prefer to keep your options open rather than make a decision as soon as possible.
You feel uneasy when you need to deviate from a well-established schedule.
When going out, you like to just go and see where the night takes you.
Once you have made a decision, you stop thinking about the other options.
You think that improvisation is key to solving problems.
When preparing for a journey, you spend time making a list of things you need to bring.
Your decisions are rarely truly final; you are always open to a change of heart.
You try to keep your workplace tidy and in order.
To you, the key to success is making yourself open to inspiration by remaining free from strict organization.
You are prone to focus on your own flaws and imperfections.
You never doubt your ability to overcome the problems you face.
Even when you make a big fool of yourself, you shrug it off and continue with your day.
You tend to overthink and stress about things.
You are able to relax and focus even under pressure.
You often think about things you could have done better long after wrapping up some work or submitting a project.
When things do not go the way you want, you tend to blame yourself.
You rarely worry things might take a turn for the worse.
